title: [18F]ZDG2 First-in-Human PET Imaging in PAH
official: First-in-Human PET Imaging of Pulmonary Vascular Remodeling in Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension Using [18F]ZDG2: Safety, Biodistribution, Dosimetry and Pharmacokinetics
summary:
The goal of this study is to find out whether \[18F\]ZDG2 can detect early blood vessel changes in people with pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). The study will help answer this question:

Can a positron emission tomography (PET) scan using \[18F\]ZDG2 help identify PAH?

Participants will:

* Receive one or two doses of the study tracer \[18F\]ZDG2 and have a PET/CT scan after each dose
* Provide blood and urine samples
* Tell the study team about any side effects or symptoms you experience
criteria:
Healthy Volunteer Criteria

Inclusion Criteria- Healthy Volunteers

1. Age 21-75 years (inclusive) at time of consent
2. Body Mass Index 18.5-35 kg/m²
3. Willing and able to provide written informed consent
4. Willing and able to comply with all study procedures
5. Able to lie flat in supine position for 60 minutes without significant discomfort
6. No history of cardiovascular disease including:

   * Symptomatic Coronary artery disease
   * Significant Valvular heart disease (stenotic or regurgative disease of moderate or grater severity)
   * Congenital heart disease
   * Symptomatic Arrhythmias
   * Pulmonary hypertension
   * Thromboembolic disease (history of recurrent pulmonary embolisms)
7. Normal baseline electrocardiogram within 28 days
8. Normal baseline echocardiogram within 6 months demonstrating:

   * Normal RV size and systolic function (Tricuspid Annular Plane Systolic Excursion\>17 mm)
   * No tricuspid regurgitation jet or estimated Right Ventricular Systolic Pressure \<35 mmHg
   * Normal Left Ventricle size and systolic function (Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction ≥50%)
   * No significant valvular disease
9. Baseline NT-proBNP \<125 pg/mL (or BNP \<50 pg/mL)
10. Non-smoker OR former smoker with quit date ≥1 year ago and \<10 pack-year history
11. For women of childbearing potential:

    -Agrees to use highly effective contraception from screening through 30 days after imaging
12. For men with Women of Childbearing Potential partners:

    * Agrees to use barrier contraception from screening through 30 days after imaging

Exclusion Criteria- Healthy Volunteers

1. Active cancer (except non-melanoma skin cancer \>2 years disease-free), metabolic encephalopathy, infection, or cardiovascular disease.
2. Active hematological, renal, pulmonary, endocrine, or hepatic disorders, except for treated thyroid disease.
3. History of pulmonary disease including:

   * Asthma
   * Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease
   * Interstitial lung disease
   * Prior pneumonia with residual changes
   * Sleep apnea
4. Participation in any investigational diagnostic or therapeutic radiopharmaceutical studies in the last year.
5. Coronary revascularization (Percutaneous Coronary Intervention or Coronary Artery Bypass Graft) within 6 months
6. Stroke or Transient Ischemic Attack within 6 months
7. Uncontrolled systemic hypertension (Systolic Blood Pressure(SBP)\>160 or Diastolic Blood Pressure(DBP)\>100 mmHg)
8. Resting systolic blood pressure \<90 mmHg
9. Clinically significant arrhythmia requiring treatment
10. Use of any prescription medication
11. Significant alcohol use (\>14 drinks/week for men, \>7 drinks/week for women)
12. Illicit drug use within 2 years (including, use of stimulants such as methamphetamine)
13. Use of amphetamine weight loss drugs
14. Portal hypertension
15. Radiation exposure \>50 mSv in the past 12 months
16. Occupational radiation exposure
17. Known genetic risk factors for PAH (ex: Bone Morphogenetic Protein Receptor Type 2 mutations)
18. History of scleroderma
19. History of pre-term birth
20. History of Human Immunodeficiency Virus
21. Known allergy or hypersensitivity to any component of the investigational product
22. Contraindication to Positron Emission Tomography / Computed Tomography imaging
23. Weight \>227 kg (500 lbs. - scanner table limit)
24. Any condition that, in the opinion of the investigator, would compromise subject safety or study data quality
25. Incarceration

PAH Patients Criteria

Inclusion Criteria- PAH Patients

1. Age 21-75 years (inclusive) at time of consent
2. Body Mass Index 18.5-40 kg/m²
3. Willing and able to provide written informed consent
4. Willing and able to comply with all study procedures
5. Able to lie flat (or semi-recumbent with 15-30° elevation) for 60 minutes
6. Confirmed diagnosis of pulmonary arterial hypertension (World Health Organization (WHO) Group 1) by right heart catheterization meeting ALL of the following hemodynamic criteria within the last 3 months:

   * Mean pulmonary artery pressure ≥20 mmHg
   * Pulmonary artery wedge pressure ≤15 mmHg
   * Pulmonary vascular resistance ≥3 Wood Units
7. PAH etiology limited to WHO Group 1 subtypes:

   * Idiopathic PAH
   * Heritable PAH
   * Drug or toxin-induced PAH
   * Associated PAH including:

     * Connective tissue disease: scleroderma, lupus, Mixed Connective Tissue Disease, etc.
     * Congenital heart disease: repaired shunts only
     * Portal hypertension
     * HIV infection
8. WHO Functional Class I, II or III:

   * Class I: No limitation of physical activity
   * Class II: Slight limitation of physical activity; ordinary activity causes symptoms
   * Class III: Marked limitation of physical activity; less than ordinary activity causes symptoms
9. 6-minute walk distance: 150-450 meters (performed with 8 weeks of screening)

   -≥150 meters: Ensures patient can complete study procedures

   -≤450 meters: Ensures meaningful disease severity for signal detection
10. Adequate organ function:

    * Creatinine Clearance ≥60 mL/min
    * AST/ALT ≤2.5× ULN
    * Total bilirubin ≤1.5× ULN
11. Clinically stable for ≥8 weeks prior to enrollment:

    * No hospitalization for PAH or heart failure
    * No PAH exacerbation or clinical worsening
    * No syncope or presyncope
    * No escalation of diuretic dose for \>2 weeks
12. Stable PAH-specific medication regimen for ≥8 weeks:

    * No addition, discontinuation, or dose change of:
    * Endothelin receptor antagonists
    * Phosphodiesterase-5 inhibitors
    * Soluble guanylate cyclase stimulators
    * Prostacyclin pathway agents
    * Activin Receptor Antagonist (Sotatercept)
13. Comprehensive echocardiogram within 8 weeks demonstrating:

    * RV size and function quantified (TAPSE, RV S')
    * Estimated RVSP documented, if adequate tricuspid regurgitation jet available
    * No severe LV dysfunction (LVEF ≥40%)
    * No more than moderate valvular disease
14. Pulmonary function tests (as measured per standard of care) within 12 months demonstrating:

    * Forced Expiratory Volume(FEV)1/Forced Vital Capacity (FVC) \>0.70 OR if \<0.70, FEV1 \>60% predicted
    * DLCO \>30% predicted
15. High-resolution chest CT (as measured per standard of care) within 12 months demonstrating:

    * No significant parenchymal lung disease (emphysema, fibrosis)
    * Enlarged main pulmonary artery typical of PH (PA diameter \>29 mm)
    * No evidence of chronic thromboembolic disease
16. Ventilation-perfusion scan (as measured per standard of care) within 12 months demonstrating:

    * Low probability OR normal study
    * No mismatched perfusion defects (excludes Chronic Thromboembolic Pulmonary Hypertension)
17. For Women Of Childbearing Potential:

    -Agrees to use highly effective contraception through 30 days after imaging
18. For men with Women Of Childbearing Potential partners:

    -Agrees to use barrier contraception through 30 days after imaging
19. Life expectancy ≥6 months in the judgment of the investigator

Exclusion Criteria- PAH Patients

1. Acute coronary syndrome within 6 months
2. Coronary revascularization (PCI or CABG) within 6 months
3. Stroke or TIA within 6 months
4. Uncontrolled systemic hypertension (SBP \>160 or DBP \>100 mmHg)
5. Resting systolic blood pressure \<90 mmHg
6. Clinically significant arrhythmia requiring treatment (except stable atrial fibrillation)
7. QTc interval value ≥ 470 msec as measured using ECG
8. Active pulmonary infection or pneumonia within 3 months
9. Pulmonary embolism (acute) within 6 months
10. Classification of other PH groups confirmed by:

    * Group 2 (LHD): PAWP ≤15 mmHg, no significant LV disease on echo
    * Group 3 (lung disease): FEV1/FVC \>0.70 OR FEV1 \>60% if obstructive; DLCO \>40% predicted; no significant interstitial lung disease on CT in the past 12 months (If no PFT available for the past 12 months patient will need one at the time of screening)
    * Group 4 (CTEPH): Ventilation-perfusion scan any time since diagnosis showing low probability or normal (no mismatched defects)
    * Group 5: No evidence of multifactorial/unclear PH mechanisms
    * For PAH: Significant Group 2, 3, 4, or 5 PH contribution
11. WHO Functional Class IV (symptoms at rest - too sick for study)
12. Radiation exposure \>50 mSv in the past 12 months
13. Occupational radiation exposure
14. Cirrhosis with portal hypertension
15. Known allergy or hypersensitivity to any component of the investigational product
16. Contraindication to PET/CT imaging
17. Weight \>227 kg (500 lbs. - scanner table limit)
18. Active malignancy (except non-melanoma skin cancer \>2 years disease-free)
19. Participation in any investigational diagnostic or therapeutic radiopharmaceutical studies in the last year.
20. Any condition that, in the opinion of the investigator, would compromise subject safety or study data quality
21. Incarceration
